product: Medical, surgical, dental and veterinary instruments (HS 9018)
local_now: No HS-9018-specific share. Kemenkes: domestic devices were 48% of device use in 2024 vs 12% in 2019 (Farmalkes, 4 Jul 2025); about 20% of ~56,000 registered devices are made locally (Bisnis, Jun 2025, snippet); 812 domestic device producers (Apr 2025). Locally certified surgical instrument sets score low TKDN (Karya Medis FIMED/HAGEN sets 24-27%, i.e. mostly imported instruments), while Marthys's CNC-made orthopaedic instrument sets score 80-86%.

cnc_3d_role: CNC: reusable stainless and titanium hand instruments (forceps, retractors, bone and orthopaedic instruments, dental hand instruments) by 5-axis milling, sliding-head turning and wire EDM, then grinding and passivation; instrument trays. 3D: patient-specific surgical guides and anatomical models printed in resin or nylon, plus jigs and prototypes. potential_share: Judgement, 3-5 years: local makers could supply about 5-10% of HS 9018 import value, US$36.9-73.9M (= 5-10% x US$738.7M), mostly reusable instrument sets and dental hand instruments sold through the TKDN-weighted e-catalogue. Reasoning: domestic devices already reached 48% of use in 2024, but local instrument sets are still largely imported (24-27% TKDN), so CNC instrument making is the open gap; Marthys shows CNC instrument sets can reach 80-86% TKDN. Limits: electromedical and disposable items dominate 9018 value and are not CNC work; the US deal (signed Feb 2026, not in force) would exempt US-origin devices (15% of 2025 imports) from TKDN preference.

product: Orthopaedic and fracture devices and artificial joints (HS 902110, 902131)
local_now: No measured market share. Marthys (Dec 2022, older than 2023) targeted ~15% share with one machine and said more machines could take it above 50%. As of Oct 2026 four makers hold TKDN certificates covering plates, screws, nails, spinal systems, external fixators and hemi-hip prostheses. Marthys alone lists about 140 product lines at 35.6-98.3% (sibling notes' registry count).

PT Risa Implantama (Surabaya)
PT Eka Ormed Indonesia (Gedangan, Sidoarjo)
PT Indonesia Teknologi Rotnhkard (Genuk, Semarang)
cnc_3d_role: CNC is the core process: sliding-head (Swiss-type) lathes for cortical, locking, cannulated and pedicle screws; 5-axis milling for locking and CMF plates; wire EDM. Risa lists CNC milling, CNC lathes, wire EDM and multi-axis machining of Ti-6Al-4V. 3D: metal powder-bed printing for patient-specific or porous implants (no local maker found) and resin or nylon printing of anatomical models and cutting guides for surgical planning.
potential_share: Judgement, 3-5 years: 30-50% of trauma devices (902110), US$10.2-17.0M (= 30-50% x US$34.0M) of 2025 import value displaced, and 5-15% of artificial joints (902131), US$0.8-2.5M (= 5-15% x US$16.9M). Reasoning: four TKDN-certified makers already cover the full trauma range (plates, screws, nails, ex-fix) at 38-98% TKDN, and the e-catalogue favours them; combined imports grew from US$34.6M (2023) to US$50.9M (2025), so demand is rising. Joints are harder: only hemi-hip/bipolar prostheses are certified locally, and surgeons prefer established brands. Limits: titanium bar is imported (Marthys, 2022); the US deal would exempt US-origin implants (25% of 2025 imports) from TKDN preference if ratified.

Hospitals doing JKN-funded trauma and spine surgery (payment rules not sourced)
Orthopaedic surgeons nationwide (Risa's stated customers)

local_now: Trade data barely captures this line (2025 imports small), because limb prostheses and orthoses are mostly fitted by local workshops as a service. TKDN-certified makers found: CV Isipa (Kota Jambi) for prosthetic legs (36%) and hands (38%); PT Pratama Sentra Rehabilitasi (Tangerang Selatan) for spinal orthoses and collars (40%); and OneMed for a truncal orthosis and cervical collar (45.05%). Searches for 'prostesis' found nothing. Indonesia also exported US$10-11M a year under 902139 in 2024-2025; the products and the exporter were not identified. The 2025 exports went to USA 39%, Singapore 20%, Germany 20%, Belgium 11%; the exporter was not identified.

product: Precious-metal jewellery (HS 7113), made with 3D-printed wax or resin patterns
local_now: Domestic supply dominates: 2025 imports were US$54.4M against exports of US$7,839.8M, so imports equal 0.7% of exports; no measured domestic market share. Exports rose 42% from 2023 to 2025 (gold-type 711319 US$7,647.4M; silver 711311 US$192.1M, up from US$104.6M). The 2025 export unit value of 711319 was about US$93,249 per kg (estimate: US$7,647.4M / 82,010 kg reported), consistent with high-carat gold pieces. Gold-type exports (711319) went to Switzerland 51%, Singapore 15%, United Arab Emirates 13%, China, Hong Kong SAR 8%; silver (711311) to Japan 47%, Thailand 22%, USA 15%, Germany 4% (2025).

cnc_3d_role: 3D: CAD-designed pieces printed as castable resin or wax patterns, then lost-wax cast. This cuts model-making time and allows short runs, personalisation and fast design cycles (UBS releases new designs every two weeks). CNC: diamond-cut faceting, engraving, ring and bangle turning; laser welding and marking. Machine-made chain and high-carat commodity pieces, likely much of the export value, use chain machines and casting rather than 3D (inference).
potential_share: Judgement, 3-5 years: the import share is already tiny, so the target is process share. About 25-50% of design-led cast pieces from Java and Bali workshops could move to CAD plus 3D-printed resin or wax patterns. Replacing 5-15% of branded 711319 imports (US$39.4M, mostly Italy, USA, Switzerland, France) would add only US$2.0-5.9M (= 5-15% x US$39.4M). Reasoning: castable-resin printing needs little capital and fits fast design cycles (UBS launches designs every two weeks). Public capacity already exists: Celuk's Kemenperin/Gianyar centre has CNC, 3D-printing and laser machines (2025), and BBKB Yogyakarta prints resin masters and casts silver as a service (2026). Kotagede needs ways to attract young artisans. High-carat commodity and machine-chain exports, likely most of the US$7.6bn, gain less from 3D. The export mix (half to Switzerland, a refining and trading hub, plus Singapore, the UAE and Hong Kong) suggests much of the gold value is high-carat, commodity-like jewellery (inference).

potential_share: Judgement, 3-5 years: 15-30% of furniture imports, US$79.9-159.7M (= 15-30% x US$532.4M), could be replaced by local CNC panel and metal-furniture makers. Reasoning: the import surge is mostly metal furniture, which is laser-, tube- and press-brake work that Java metal shops can do; government and school furniture is bought by TKDN (e.g. Solobeat 43-64%). On exports, CNC mainly defends share: exports were flat to down 2023-2025, the US (57% of 2025 exports) has charged 19% on Indonesian goods since the July 2025 framework, furniture is not on the 0% list of the Feb 2026 deal, and IEU-CEPA is not yet in force.

product: Guitars and other string and electric instruments (HS 9202, 9207)
local_now: Export platform: 2025 exports US$454.9M (9202 US$70.7M, 9207 US$384.1M, which includes electric keyboards) against imports of US$14.6M. Cort/Cor-Tek, Samick, Yamaha and Ibanez-brand guitars are made in Indonesia. Instrument parts imports (9209) were US$127.4M, a sign that hardware and electronics are imported. No measured domestic share. In US import data for 2025, Indonesia supplied 30% of electric guitars and similar (920790; first place), 15% of acoustic string instruments (920290) and 27% of electric keyboards (920710).

Indonesia's existing US share (30% of 920790 imports, 15% of 920290) shows the OEM base is already competitive; growth depends on brand owners shifting more volume from China and Mexico (inference).

Six of 12 Turkish Anka MALE drones (ordered Feb 2023, US$300M) are to be assembled by Indonesian Aerospace (PTDI). PTDI's own Elang Hitam MALE drone is still in development. 2025 drone exports (US$11.6M) went to Poland 82%, China, Hong Kong SAR 14%, China 1%, Saudi Arabia 1%; the exporter was not identified.

product: Small household appliances and their housings (HS 8516 electro-thermic, 8509 food processors and mixers, 841451 fans); consumer-electronics enclosures are not separately visible
local_now: Two-way trade: 2025 imports US$643.7M against exports of US$771.6M. Exports rose 81% from 2023 (US$425.7M), led by coffee and tea makers (851671, US$315.7M), irons (851640, US$119.0M) and food processors (850940, US$105.5M, up from US$4.7M). Domestic brands certify TKDN of only 17-40% (Maspion, Star Cosmos, Miyako maker Kencana Gemilang, and SCNP's Turbo and Philips blenders). Import origins 2025: China 82%, Viet Nam 6%, China, Hong Kong SAR 3%, Malaysia 2%. Export destinations: 8516 USA 52%, Netherlands 6%, France 6%, Hungary 5%; 8509 USA 87%, Canada 3%, Hungary 2%, Mexico 1%.
